matrix.headline: PostHog, Google Tag Manager and Google Ads fire before any consent interaction
matrix.reasoning: On the site, a PostHog cookie and requests to Google Tag Manager and Google Ads are seen before any consent interaction, and PostHog, Google Tag Manager and Google Ads receive usage data, device ID, IP address and, for PostHog, email address. Because Google Ads is advertising and PostHog and Google Tag Manager also record sessions, the statistical-purposes exception is unlikely to cover them, so a possible inconsistency with PECR reg. 6(1) and Schedule A1 para. 5 arises; that exception would only apply if the sole purpose were statistics about how the site is used, the data were not shared with anyone else except to help improve it, clear information were given and a simple, free means of objecting existed. Separately, user content is sent to OpenAI for AI features while the policy does not mention AI, machine learning or automated processing, a possible inconsistency with UK GDPR Art. 13(1)(c) as to the stated purposes and legal basis.

fixes.policy_clause: We use AI features powered by OpenAI to process content you submit, such as messages and document or data-room text, so that we can generate titles, draft replies and build data-room structures. The legal basis we rely on for this processing is [legal basis].

We use PostHog for product analytics and Google Tag Manager and Google Ads for analytics and advertising. These tools may set cookies and collect your usage data, device ID, IP address and email address before you interact with our consent banner. We ask for your consent before these tools run, and you can withdraw it at any time via [consent settings link].
fixes.code_change: Load PostHog, Google Tag Manager and Google Ads tags only after consent is recorded (e.g. gate the PostHog init and the GTM container in the site layout/consent provider, and remove the pre-consent `ph_phc_..._posthog` and `_gcl_au` cookies).

matrix.headline: User content sent to OpenAI for AI features but policy is silent on AI processing
matrix.reasoning: Code shows user content passed to OpenAI in chat title generation (generate-chat-title.ts:16), message sending (send-message.ts:390) and AI dataroom structure generation (generate-ai-structure.ts:109), while the privacy policy does not mention AI, machine learning or automated processing at all. Under ICO Guidance on AI and data protection, Transparency in AI, organisations are expected to tell people when and how their personal data is processed by AI systems, so the silence in the policy is a possible inconsistency with that expectation. Because the UK has no AI-specific statute and this rests on regulator guidance rather than legislation, the cell is capped at amber.

fixes.policy_clause: We use artificial intelligence to power certain features, such as generating chat titles and document room structures. When you use these features, the content you provide is sent to our AI provider, OpenAI, and processed to generate the result. You can choose not to use these features if you prefer not to have your content processed in this way.

fixes.code_change: Ensure user content sent to OpenAI in ee/features/ai/lib/chat/generate-chat-title.ts, ee/features/ai/lib/chat/send-message.ts and pages/api/teams/[teamId]/datarooms/generate-ai-structure.ts is limited to what the feature needs, and add a comment at each call site noting the AI processing so the privacy review stays current.

matrix.headline: PostHog, Google Tag Manager and Google Ads fire before any consent interaction
matrix.reasoning: Cookie and network evidence shows PostHog, Google Tag Manager and Google Ads requests and cookies (including `_gcl_au`) set on the site before any consent interaction, with usage data, device ID, IP address and, for PostHog, email address collected. The UK statistical-purposes exception does not extend to advertising or session-recording trackers, so it would only be relevant to strictly statistical analytics; it cannot cover Google Ads here. This may be a possible inconsistency with s. 225 (unfair commercial practices, including misleading omissions), because visitors may not be told about, or asked to agree to, tracking that starts on arrival. Outcomes would turn on whether the site clearly and prominently discloses these pre-consent trackers and their purposes.

fixes.policy_clause: We use PostHog for product analytics and Google Tag Manager and Google Ads for analytics and advertising. These tools may set cookies and receive your usage data, device ID, IP address and, for PostHog, your email address, and they may begin before you interact with our consent banner. You can opt out at any time via [opt-out link], and we keep this data for [retention period].
fixes.code_change: Gate PostHog, Google Tag Manager and Google Ads (gtm.js, gtag/js, doubleclick collect) behind the consent banner: do not load or fire them until the user has given consent, in the site's tag/consent loading module.

fixes.policy_clause: Where we rely on consent for analytics and advertising cookies, we ask for it before those cookies are set, and we explain that refusing consent does not prevent you from using the site.
fixes.code_change: Ensure the consent banner defaults to no trackers and that refusing consent leaves PostHog and Google tags unloaded; add a test asserting no requests to googletagmanager.com, doubleclick.net or PostHog before consent.

matrix.headline: PostHog, Google Tag Manager, Google Ads fire before consent; OpenAI gets user content
matrix.reasoning: Non-essential trackers from PostHog, Google Tag Manager and Google Ads are seen setting cookies and making requests on papermark.com before any consent interaction, and they receive usage data, device ID and IP address (PostHog also email address). Under Directive 2002/58/EC Art. 5(3), storing or accessing information on a device needs prior consent unless strictly necessary to provide a requested service, and without a valid legal basis under Regulation Art. 6(1) the consent requirements of Regulation Art. 7 apply, including being able to demonstrate consent. Separately, user content is passed to OpenAI for AI features while the privacy policy does not mention AI, machine learning or automated processing, which is a possible inconsistency with the information duty in Regulation Art. 13(1)(c) on purposes and legal basis.

fixes.policy_clause: We load analytics and advertising technologies, including PostHog, Google Tag Manager and Google Ads, only after you have given consent through our cookie banner. Until then, no non-essential cookies or trackers are set and no usage data, device ID or IP address is sent to these providers. You can withdraw your consent at any time with the same ease as giving it.
fixes.code_change: Gate PostHog initialization, the Google Tag Manager container (GTM-WH2DMPB6) and the Google Ads tag (AW-17198795665) behind the consent state in the site's consent manager so no script, cookie or network request fires before consent is recorded.

fixes.policy_clause: We use OpenAI to power AI features such as generating document room structures and chat titles. When you use these features, the content you provide is sent to OpenAI for processing on our behalf for that purpose. Our legal basis for this processing is [legal basis].

If you do not consent to analytics and advertising cookies, we do not run PostHog, Google Tag Manager or Google Ads on your device, and we do not sell or share your usage data, device ID or IP address with them for advertising.

matrix.headline: User content goes to OpenAI for AI features while the policy never mentions AI processing
matrix.reasoning: Code evidence shows user content being sent to OpenAI (US) from the chat title, chat message and data room AI-structure features (generate-chat-title.ts, send-message.ts, generate-ai-structure.ts). The privacy policy does not mention AI, machine learning or automated processing at all, so people interacting with these features are not told, in the policy, that they are interacting with an AI system. That combination may be a possible inconsistency with Art. 50(1), which requires that people be informed they are interacting with an AI system unless that is obvious from the context; whether the exception applies depends on how the interface presents these features to the user.

fixes.policy_clause: Some features of our service are powered by AI. When you use our AI chat and data room structure features, the content you enter (such as your messages and documents) is sent to our AI provider, OpenAI, so that it can generate a response or a suggested structure. We also use OpenAI to generate short titles for your AI chats. When you use these features, you are interacting with an AI system rather than a person.
We label AI-generated output and AI-driven interfaces so that you can tell when you are interacting with an AI system.
fixes.code_change: In ee/features/ai/lib/chat/send-message.ts and ee/features/ai/lib/chat/generate-chat-title.ts, keep the existing in-product AI disclosure visible (do not remove it to rely on the policy alone).

matrix.headline: PostHog, Google Tag Manager and Google Ads trackers fire before any consent
matrix.reasoning: Cookie and network evidence from www.papermark.com shows PostHog, Google Tag Manager and Google Ads being set or contacted before any consent interaction, and these recipients receive usage data, device ID and IP address (PostHog also receives email address). Under the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive, Art. 5, this may be a possible inconsistency with the requirement of professional diligence if the average consumer's economic behaviour is materially distorted, or is likely to be materially distorted, by tracking that begins before they are given a choice. Whether that threshold is met would depend on the nature, timing and visibility of the pre-consent tracking and on its effect on consumer decisions.

fixes.policy_clause: Before any non-essential cookies or tracking technologies are set, we ask for your consent. Until you consent, we do not load PostHog, Google Tag Manager or Google Ads on our site. If you consent, PostHog may receive usage data, device ID, IP address and email address, and Google Tag Manager and Google Ads may receive usage data, device ID and IP address. You can withdraw your consent at any time via [consent settings link], and we keep consent records for [retention period].
fixes.code_change: Gate the PostHog and Google Tag Manager initialisation scripts (and the Google Ads gtag/DoubleClick conversions) behind the consent state: do not load or call them until the consent interaction resolves to granted, e.g. in the site's analytics/marketing bootstrap module replace the eager script injection and the ph_phc_* cookie creation with calls that run only after the consent callback, and set the _gcl_au cookie only after consent.

matrix.headline: PostHog, Google Ads and 1 more fire before consent; user content goes to OpenAI
matrix.reasoning: Code shows user content being passed to OpenAI for AI features, while the privacy policy does not mention AI, machine learning or automated processing, so users may not be told about this processing or its cross-border transfer to a US provider. Separately, cookies and network requests for PostHog, Google Tag Manager and Google Ads (usage data, device ID, IP address, email address) are seen on the site before any consent interaction. Under Art. 7, collection, transfer to third parties and cross-border transfer require the subject's consent unless a case set by law applies, so the timing of these analytics and advertising requests may be a possible inconsistency with Art. 7. Kazakhstan has no cookie-specific rule, so the general consent requirement in Art. 7 is the relevant standard.

This may involve transfer of your content outside Kazakhstan. We do not include your AI inputs in our own model training.

We use PostHog for product analytics, and Google Tag Manager and Google Ads for analytics and advertising. These providers may receive your usage data, device ID, IP address and email address. We ask for your consent before these tools are loaded and, where you do not consent, we do not set the associated cookies or make the associated requests.
fixes.code_change: Gate PostHog, Google Tag Manager and Google Ads (gtag config, AW-17198795665 and the DoubleClick collect call) behind the consent banner so no script, cookie (`ph_phc_...`, `_gcl_au`) or network request fires in `pages/_app.tsx`/document head until the user has given consent.

fixes.policy_clause: [Retention period] We keep the data described above only for as long as needed for the purposes stated, after which we delete or anonymise it.

matrix.headline: User content sent to OpenAI for AI features; policy never mentions AI
matrix.reasoning: Code shows user content passed to OpenAI in the chat title generator, the message sender and the AI data-room structure generator, while the privacy policy does not mention AI, machine learning or automated processing at all. Under Art. 21(1) users must be informed that goods, works and services are produced or provided using AI systems, and Art. 16(1) gives users rights to read the AI system's user agreement, to data protection, to explanations of results affecting their rights, and to refuse non-mandatory interaction. The policy's silence means these notices and rights are not reflected in the text; whether Art. 16(1) and Art. 21(1) require action here would depend on whether the AI features are treated as services provided using AI systems and, for the refusal right, whether interaction is mandatory by law.

fixes.policy_clause: We use artificial intelligence systems, including OpenAI, to provide some of our features. When you use these features, the content you provide (such as your messages, prompts and document text) is sent to OpenAI so that it can generate results, for example chat titles, replies and suggested data room structures. We tell you when a result is produced by an AI system, we explain, on request, how a result that affects your rights was produced, and you can choose not to interact with these AI features where that interaction is not required by law. We keep the content sent to OpenAI for [retention period] and handle it in accordance with our data protection obligations.

You have the right to read the terms that apply to our AI features, to the protection of your personal data processed by them, to an explanation of results that affect your rights, and to refuse to interact with an AI system where that interaction is not mandatory by law. To exercise these rights, contact us at [contact email].

fixes.code_change: In ee/features/ai/lib/chat/generate-chat-title.ts:16, ee/features/ai/lib/chat/send-message.ts:390 and pages/api/teams/[teamId]/datarooms/generate-ai-structure.ts:109, show an in-product AI notice before user content is sent to OpenAI, and record that the notice was shown.

matrix.headline: PostHog, Google Tag Manager and Google Ads fire before any consent interaction
matrix.reasoning: The site sets a PostHog cookie and sends requests to Google Tag Manager and Google Ads (including advertising requests) before any consent interaction. PostHog receives usage data, device ID, IP address and email address, while Google Tag Manager and Google Ads receive usage data, device ID and IP address. Kazakhstan has no cookie-specific rule, so general consent requirements for collection apply, and the absence of consumer-facing information at the point where these trackers run creates a possible inconsistency with the consumer's right to full, reliable and timely information under Art. 10. This is not legal advice.

fixes.policy_clause: We use PostHog, Google Tag Manager and Google Ads to understand how our site is used and to measure our advertising. These tools may collect your usage data, device ID, IP address and, for PostHog, your email address, and may set cookies on your device. Where these tools run before you make a choice, we tell you about it in the banner shown on your first visit, and you can [accept/decline] before the tools load.
fixes.code_change: Defer loading of PostHog, Google Tag Manager (GTM-WH2DMPB6, AW-17198795665) and Google Ads/Doubleclick tags until the visitor makes a consent choice; gate the snippet that sets `ph_phc_..._posthog` and `_gcl_au` behind the consent state.

fixes.policy_clause: We provide clear information about the cookies and analytics and advertising tools used on this site (including PostHog, Google Tag Manager and Google Ads), what data they collect, and how you can contact us with questions about this processing. UK-PECR-6.instrument: Privacy and Electronic Communications (EC Directive) Regulations 2003 (PECR)
UK-PECR-6.ref: reg. 6(1), as substituted by Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 s. 112
UK-PECR-6.title: Storing or accessing information on a user's device
UK-PECR-6.summary: A person must not store information, or gain access to information stored, in a user's terminal equipment unless an exception in Schedule A1 applies (for example consent, or strict necessity).

UK-PECR-SCHA1-5.instrument: PECR Schedule A1, inserted by Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 Sch. 12
UK-PECR-SCHA1-5.title: Statistical-purposes exception for analytics cookies
UK-PECR-SCHA1-5.summary: Consent is not required where the sole purpose of the storage or access is to collect information for statistical purposes about how the service or website is used, with a view to improving it, provided the information is not shared with anyone else except to help make those improvements, the user is given clear and comprehensive information about the purpose, and the user is given a simple, free means of objecting and does not object.

UK-GDPR-13-1-c.instrument: UK GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679 as retained in UK law)
UK-GDPR-13-1-c.title: Purposes and legal basis must be disclosed
UK-GDPR-13-1-c.summary: When collecting data from the person, the controller must state the purposes of the processing and its legal basis.

UK-ICO-AI-GUIDANCE.instrument: ICO Guidance on AI and data protection (regulator guidance, not statute)
UK-ICO-AI-GUIDANCE.title: Be transparent about AI processing of personal data
UK-ICO-AI-GUIDANCE.summary: The UK has no AI-specific statute. ICO guidance expects organisations to tell people when and how their personal data is processed by AI systems, as part of UK GDPR transparency.

UK-DMCC-225.instrument: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024, Part 4 Chapter 1
UK-DMCC-225.title: Prohibition of unfair commercial practices
UK-DMCC-225.summary: Unfair commercial practices are prohibited, including misleading actions, misleading omissions and practices that contravene professional diligence.

EU-EPRIVACY-5-3.instrument: Directive 2002/58/EC (ePrivacy Directive), as amended by Directive 2009/136/EC
EU-EPRIVACY-5-3.title: Consent for cookies and similar technologies
EU-EPRIVACY-5-3.summary: Storing information, or accessing information stored, on a user's device is only allowed with the user's consent after clear information, unless strictly necessary to provide a service the user requested.

EU-GDPR-7.title: Conditions for consent
EU-GDPR-7.summary: Where processing relies on consent, the controller must be able to demonstrate that the person consented, and consent must be as easy to withdraw as to give.

EU-GDPR-6.title: Lawful basis for processing
EU-GDPR-6.summary: Processing is lawful only if at least one legal basis applies, such as consent, contract, legal obligation or legitimate interests.

EU-GDPR-13-1-c.title: Purposes and legal basis must be disclosed
EU-GDPR-13-1-c.summary: When collecting data from the person, the controller must state the purposes of the processing and its legal basis.

EU-AIACT-50-1.title: People must be told they are interacting with an AI system
EU-AIACT-50-1.summary: Providers must ensure AI systems intended to interact directly with people are designed so that people are informed they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from the context.

EU-UCPD-5.title: Prohibition of unfair commercial practices
EU-UCPD-5.summary: Unfair commercial practices are prohibited: practices contrary to professional diligence that materially distort, or are likely to materially distort, the economic behaviour of the average consumer.

KZ-PD-7.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V 'On Personal Data and their Protection' (21 May 2013)
KZ-PD-7.title: Conditions for collection and processing
KZ-PD-7.summary: Collection and processing of personal data is carried out with the consent of the subject, except in cases set by law. Transfer to third parties and cross-border transfer are subject to consent.

KZ-AI-16.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 230-VIII 'On Artificial Intelligence' (17 November 2025, in force 18 January 2026)
KZ-AI-16.title: User rights when interacting with AI systems
KZ-AI-16.summary: Users have the right to read the user agreement of the AI system, to protection of their personal data processed by it, to explanations of results affecting their rights, and to refuse to interact with an AI system where interaction is not mandatory by law.

KZ-AI-21-1.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 230-VIII 'On Artificial Intelligence' (17 November 2025, in force 18 January 2026)
KZ-AI-21-1.title: Users must be informed that AI is used
KZ-AI-21-1.summary: Users must be informed that goods, works and services are produced or provided using artificial intelligence systems.

KZ-CP-10.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 274-IV 'On Protection of Consumer Rights' (4 May 2010)
KZ-CP-10.title: Consumer right to information
KZ-CP-10.summary: The consumer has the right to receive full, reliable and timely information about goods, works and services and about the seller or provider.
